title: Deep Active and Passive Geophysical Investigation at the Vettabbia Site (Milan, Italy) and Implications for Site-Specific Earthquake Ground Response Analysis
content: This work presents a new detailed seismo-stratigraphic model for a target site located South East of Milan (Italy) and obtained from geological data, single-station and 2D-seismic passive measurements and a high-quality deep seismic reflection profile. The study is an improvement on Massa et al. (2022), which investigates the spatial variability of the local seismic site response of the deep alluvial deposits in the Milan area. The work aims to augment the usefulness in merging passive and active geophysical surveys to better depict the stratigraphic discontinuities for a detailed shear waves velocity (Vs) profile. New active geophysical data were acquired during 2023 through a 1.5 km high-resolution reflection profile at Vettabbia site (South of Milan), using 240, 4.5 Hz-geophones. The compressive velocity profile and the discontinuity depths were merged with Massa et al. (2022) constraints to better fix the joint inversion of the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and ellipticity curves, and obtain a reliable Vs profile deeper than ~1.0 km. A site-specific earthquake ground response analysis was estimated through 1D equivalent-linear numerical models. Seismic inputs were selected considering the reference spectra of the Italian building-code (2018). The results show relevant resonance peaks from 1 to 4 Hz, in agreement with earthquake HVSRs of Massa et al. (2022), while at frequencies < 1 Hz the numerical models show smoothed amplification. The interdisciplinary processing scheme might provide a reference for future site characterisation in urban areas, informing both urban planning and earthquake risk reduction strategies.
